findings.title: Exit code for recreate changed and old value repurposed
findings.body: This change moves RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and assigns FEATURE_DISABLED to 4. The documentation tells users to rely on these exit codes for automation, so existing scripts or tests written against the previous runtime behavior may now misinterpret exit code 4 as feature-disabled rather than recreate, and recreate results will move to 3. If this is intentional, it should be clearly noted as a behavior change; otherwise a new unused exit code should be chosen for the feature-disabled case.

findings.title: Documented exit codes are not asserted in tests
findings.body: The tests only assert message text, not exit codes, even though the PR introduces/changes documented exit codes: 0 for compatible, 3 for recreate-required, and 4 for feature disabled. For example, testFeatureNotEnabled should assert exit code 4 and testWrongVersions should assert exit code 3, and the successful check path should assert 0. Without these assertions, regressions in the exit-code contract would not be caught.

findings.title: Enabled features are overwritten instead of preserved
findings.body: setEnabledFeatures(List.of(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())) replaces any existing enabled features in the FeatureSpec. If the shared test deployment setup already enables other features, this test will silently disable them when testing the RECREATE strategy, potentially changing test behavior or causing unrelated failures. Adding the feature to the existing list would be safer.

findings.title: Feature-flag caution is ambiguous for default update behavior
findings.body: The caution states that the operator will fail if the rolling-updates feature is not enabled, but the same section also documents a default <not set> behavior, and the UpgradeTest exercises a null update strategy without enabling the feature. If the feature is only required when spec.update or an explicit strategy is used, the documentation should say that explicitly; otherwise the statement is inconsistent with the described default behavior and tests.
